security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown fences and TypeScript template strings in instructional examples. One medium operational risk remains because the skill includes shell commands for package installation and scanners. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: The local node scanner command can execute repository code.
remediation.suggestion: Advise users to inspect xss-scanner.js or use a trusted scanner before running local scripts.

content.user_title: Scan Frontend Code for XSS Risks
content.value_statement: Frontend XSS issues are easy to miss during normal code review. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused checks for unsafe rendering, URL handling, and sanitization gaps.
actual_capabilities: Reviews frontend code for innerHTML, outerHTML, document.write, and insertAdjacentHTML usage.
Checks React components for dangerouslySetInnerHTML and missing DOMPurify sanitization.
Checks Vue templates for v-html usage and safer text rendering alternatives.
Flags URL assignment patterns that may allow javascript: or data: payloads.
Recommends safer patterns such as textContent, URL validation, and DOMPurify sanitization.
Produces a severity-based XSS report with fixes and prevention guidance.
limitations: It is guidance and sample scanner logic, not a packaged executable scanner.
String-based examples can miss complex data flow and framework-specific escapes.
Findings need human review before security decisions or release blocking.
Optional command examples require local tool setup and user approval.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge XSS review
use_cases.description: Review changed frontend files before merging a feature that renders user content.

use_cases.title: Framework security audit
use_cases.description: Check React, Vue, or Angular code for unsafe rendering and sanitizer bypass patterns.

use_cases.title: Secure coding guidance
use_cases.description: Create clear remediation notes for teams that need safer DOM and URL handling patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Basic XSS scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small component or file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this frontend file for XSS risks. Focus on unsafe HTML rendering, URL assignments, and missing sanitization. Return findings with severity and fixes.

prompt_templates.title: React rendering review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of React components that render rich content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these React components for dangerouslySetInnerHTML, raw HTML helpers, and unsafe props. Explain each risk and suggest safer React patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Framework migration audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across React, Vue, Angular, and plain JavaScript files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this frontend directory for XSS risks across frameworks. Group findings by file, severity, source of input, rendering sink, and recommended mitigation.

prompt_templates.title: Release security report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an XSS release review report from these findings. Include risk impact, affected patterns, required fixes, safe examples, and items that need manual validation.

output_examples.input: A React component renders article HTML received from an API.
output_examples.output: The report flags unsafe rich HTML rendering, rates it high severity, and recommends DOMPurify before rendering.

output_examples.input: A Vue template uses v-html for user profile content.
output_examples.output: The review identifies raw HTML rendering, explains the XSS path, and recommends v-text or sanitized HTML.

output_examples.input: A JavaScript redirect uses a query parameter as the destination.
output_examples.output: The result warns about unsafe URL assignment and recommends protocol allowlisting with the URL constructor.

best_practices: Review every finding with the surrounding data flow before blocking a release.
Prefer safe rendering APIs such as textContent unless trusted HTML is required.
Require explicit approval before running package installs, Semgrep, or local scanner scripts.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every innerHTML occurrence as exploitable without checking sanitization.
Do not approve raw HTML rendering because the source appears internal.
Do not run local scanner scripts from an untrusted repository without review.

faq.question: Does this skill run a scanner automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides review steps, sample scanner logic, and optional command examples.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers React, Vue, Angular guidance, and plain JavaScript DOM patterns.

faq.question: Can it prove that code is free of XSS?
faq.answer: No. It can find risky patterns, but human review and testing are still required.

faq.question: Does it recommend DOMPurify?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends DOMPurify for cases where trusted HTML rendering is required.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it on a repository?
faq.answer: Yes. They can use the checklist and prompts to review frontend files in a repository.

faq.question: Are the command examples safe to run?
faq.answer: They should be reviewed first. Package installs and local scripts need explicit user approval.
